headings.title: SMTO-TSK-0059 — The Agent's plan has steps waiting on each other in a loop

html:
SMTO-TSK-0059 — The Agent's plan has steps waiting on each other in a loop

GUID: 460adad1-5de5-4605-8c8e-b6137fc37849
Slug: dependency-graph-invalid
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The Agent planned steps that wait for one another, but some point to a step that doesn't exist, to themselves, or wait on each other in a circle. SMTO rejected the plan, so none of its steps ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait to see whether the Agent tries again with a corrected plan; it is told about this problem automatically. The Agent usually fixes the order of its steps on its next attempt.
  2. If the task ends with this error, send a message asking the Agent to continue and do the steps one after another in a clear order. A plain sequence has no loops, and none of the rejected steps ran, so nothing is repeated.
  3. If it keeps happening, open Options under the message box and turn off Dependency-aware scheduling before sending your next message. With it off, the Agent doesn't plan linked steps, so this kind of loop can't happen.

What success looks like

  • The Agent's steps start in order and show results in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending the same request unchanged; the Agent may plan it the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Graph validation rejected the batch because a depends_on edge names an unknown or out-of-scope alias, a node depends on itself, or the edges form a cycle with no valid topological order.

What this means

  • A graph edge names an unknown alias, points to itself or leaves no valid topological ordering because of a cycle. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • A graph edge names an unknown alias, points to itself or leaves no valid topological ordering because of a cycle.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect new and retained node aliases and graph cycles before admission.

How to fix it

  • Correct the depends_on references so each names an existing node id or activity id in this run, remove self-references, and break any cycle. Previously accepted nodes cannot be redefined; append new nodes that depend on them instead.
  • Correct dependency references and remove cycles without redefining accepted work. No affected activities were started by this validation failure.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Every dependency refers to an accepted in-scope node and the graph has an acyclic order.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
